chunks: A group narrated it from Uthman ibn Abi Shayba, and Abdullah ibn Umar ibn Sa'id al-Ashajj, and Abu Kurayb, and Mahmud ibn Ghaylan, and Ali ibn Muhammad, and Ibraheem ibn Sa'id; they all said: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Mujalid, from ash-Sha'bi, from Masruq.

He said: A man came to Abdullah ibn Mas'ood and asked him: 'Did your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) tell you how many caliphs would be after him?' He said: 'Yes, and no one has asked me about it before you, and you are the youngest of the people in age.' He said: 'After me, there will be as many as the chieftains of Moses.'
ai.seo_question: How many caliphs did the Prophet say would follow him according to the narration of Abdullah ibn Mas'ood?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the Sunni tradition of the twelve caliphs by linking the Prophet's promise to the twelve chieftains of Moses, a typology deeply resonant in Shia exegesis regarding the twelve Imams. Ibn Mas'ood’s specific mention of the man's youth underscores the transmission of this eschatological knowledge to the early generations, reinforcing the continuity of divine guidance. The reference to 'nuqaba' (chieftains) serves as a direct Quranic anchor for the concept of divinely appointed leadership succeeding the Prophet.
